asr.full_text: A solemn walaikum. About 2,400 years ago, a physician named Hippocrates was working on a disease which was until then called apoplexy. He was that great physician whom the world later accepted as the father of medicine. This physician wanted to prove to the world that evil spirits are not behind everything, rather there are many diseases that exist in the world which are caused by germs and their proper treatment can be discovered. He wanted to bring the world from superstitions to scientific studies and this thinking of his brought many revolutions in medical science, one of which is the discovery of stroke. 2400 years ago, the world believe that when any person comes under the grip of a stroke his body becomes paralyzed and this condition is called apoplexy. But Hippocrates proved to the world that paralysis is not caused by apoplexy but by a disease called stroke. The body becomes paralyzed due to it. So let us now understand stroke disease in detail. Stroke is the name of the condition in which blood supply to the brain tissues is not possible and as a result, specific tissues of the brain die. Usually the blood clot forms in the vessels which does not allow the blood to reach the brain tissues. For some common symptons of brain stroke, I will tell you one key word and that is FAST FIRST Here F stands for Facebook In stroke, one side of the patient's face droops uselessly. droops means bending downwards. Such patients are unable to smile and cannot move their face either. A stands for arm. The patient's arms become weak and he cannot lift his arms up. S stands for speech. Such patients are not able to pronounce proper words and sentences. Such patients have a lot of problem in speaking. T stands for time. As soon as you see such a patient, immediately dial the emergency number and call an ambulance and do not waste any time. Apart from these symptoms, there are many other symptoms of stroke which include headache, trouble in walking and paralysis etc. Two major causes of stroke include blocked artery and narrowing of blood vessel. When stroke occurs due to blocked artery, this condition is called ischemic stroke. In ischemic stroke, a clot forms in the blood vessel carrying blood to the brain. This clot is formed either due to fatty deposits or due to deposition of some other type of debris. Due to this clot, either the blood vessel becomes very narrow or gets completely blocked and the supply of blood to the brain tissues stops completely. Another type of stroke is transient ischemic stroke. It is a temporary stroke whose symptoms are more or less similar to ischemic stroke. It does not permanently damage the brain tissues but is a short term stroke if we look at the risk factors that develop stroke in our body then these include obesity physical inactivity heavy drinking illegal drugs high blood pressure high cholesterol cigarette smoking covid19 infection and cardiovascular diseases, etc. People whose age is more than 55 years. They also have higher chances of stroke. Men have more chances of stroke than women. However, stroke produces some permanent disabilities in the body. These complications include paralysis . If we talk about Stroke Prevention, then these include controlling blood pressure, reducing the amount of cholesterol in your diet, quitting smoking, losing weight, regular exercise and avoiding illegal drugs, etc. Many medicines are given to the patient for the treatment of stroke. These include aspirin, anti-platelets, anticoagulants, blood pressure medicines and sadhns, etc. Aspirin is a pain killer that plays the role of pain relievers in the body. The function of anti-platelets and anticoagulants is to prevent blood plots the medicines given as blood pressure medicines include alpha and beta blockers calcium channel blockers and thiazide diuretics etcetera the common function of all these medicines is to maintain blood pressure statin medicines reduce cholesterol levels in the Body Doctors perform surgery in many serious stroke patients. This surgical process is called Kaeraneotomy. In this process, a portion of the skull is removed and then the damaged blood vessel is replaced or the clot is removed. After performing the operation, the bone removed from the skull is reinserted into the skull and in this way the patient recovers. So hope u must have learned something new from today's video. Before leaving, Please Subscribe to our second Youtube Channel Saad Khan TV. Thank you. Allah Hafiz.
